source.title: SmoothOut: Smoothing Out Sharp Minima for Generalization in Large-Batch Deep Learning
source.authors: W. Wen; Yan-Dan Wang; Feng Yan; Cong Xu; Chun-Peng Wu; Yi-Ran Chen; H. Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; minor PDF extraction artifacts do not prevent reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether a noise-based intervention that changes sharpness also changes the training-to-validation generalization gap, using its own experiments and sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: Reports results for SmoothOut/AdaSmoothOut and ablations on CIFAR, MNIST, and ImageNet. Related-work statements about large-batch gaps, dropout, and other methods are cited claims, not this study's results. Sharpness values and accuracy results in Tables I–V are included; figures are used only where the text describes the result.
record.test_reason: The study repeats the large-versus-small-batch accuracy comparison using Keskar-style benchmarks and reports an explicit fixed-epoch AlexNet comparison. These results test V5. Its sharpness experiments do not establish V7's specified relationship with training–test error gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SmoothOut and AdaSmoothOut encourage flatter minima and improve held-out accuracy in their tested small- and large-batch settings, including when combined with selected existing training techniques.
record.recipe_differences: Adds noise perturbation and denoising during training, with an adaptive variant scaling noise by filter norm; evaluates accuracy and (Cε, A)-sharpness rather than testing the original study's batch-size intervention alone.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with dataset, architecture, batch size, epoch count, learning-rate scaling, noise type, and whether noise is adapted to filter norm or denoised. The authors report that the preferred learning-rate scaling rule depends on dataset and network.

fits_no_version.finding: SmoothOut and AdaSmoothOut improve accuracy over fixed-large-batch baselines on ResNet44 and ResNet18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise injection with denoising can improve held-out accuracy at a fixed batch size; matched small-batch references are needed to quantify batch-penalty recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: The tested interventions reduce measured sharpness or noise sensitivity while improving held-out accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these networks and interventions, flatter measured minima accompany higher held-out accuracy.

record.problems: The experiments focus on selected networks and settings, mostly report accuracy rather than training and test error together, and the stated sharpness measurement uses an estimation algorithm that may fail to find the exact maximum. The paper reports using the maximum of five measurements. Some plotted sensitivity results are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: No required result rows omitted. Figure-only values in Figures 2, 5–9 were not reconstructed numerically; Figure 2's C1/CIFAR-10 noise-sensitivity illustration is described in the text but does not provide a direct measure for V7's magnitude-aware generalization-gap claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local-connectivity explanations.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons under controlled tuning.
Language models, a sweep locating the workload-dependent batch threshold, and matched small-batch comparisons for the ResNet experiments. Table I does not explicitly establish fixed epoch budgets.
Controlled dropout addition or removal, small-training-set dependence and excessive-dropout underfitting.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test error gaps among comparably fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

missing.what: AlexNet small-batch top-1 accuracy of 56.15% at batch 256, with the same 60-epoch budget as the 47.64% large-batch baseline. This supplies the direct fixed-epoch batch comparison missing from R7.
missing.locator: Section IV-B, ImageNet discussion following Table II

record.verdict_notes: No challenges or scope-limiting verdict follows from untested tasks or missing comparators. The study is not an original source for V5. Sharpness results concern a related claim and do not justify a V7 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization comparisons.
Tests large versus small batch in selected networks and datasets, and reports how SmoothOut changes accuracy; does not test language models or compare all listed recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects are discussed as related work; the paper does not report a dropout intervention result.
Does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness with norm- and margin-based measures or test the stated Jiang et al. ranking claim.
